implications.impact_on_q1_q3: Q1/Q2 become a present-biased inventory/classification; longitudinal claims about organizational ecology are weakest.
implications.interpretation_limit: Do not read source-year concentration as growth in organizations or mobilization.
implications.local_gap_action: Retrieve pre-web newsletters, local newspaper holdings, flyers and organization files for 1972-2012.
implications.online_gap_action: Search web archives, historical organization histories, court/legal databases and digitized newspaper indexes by former names.
implications.visibility_mechanism: Current official and organization pages survive and are searchable; early informal groups and renamed organizations leave thinner web traces.

implications.impact_on_q1_q3: Q3 and comparisons among Henoko, Futenma, Kadena, Yonaguni, Ishigaki and Miyako are not symmetric.
implications.interpretation_limit: Place counts are observed actor-place pairs, not event frequency, local support or organizational density.
implications.local_gap_action: Prioritize Sakishima and base-adjacent local newspaper archives, council records, referendum materials and physical notices.
implications.observed_skew: Henoko 45 plus Okinawa Prefecture 37 = 82/130 actor-place observations.
implications.online_gap_action: Deepen municipal minutes, local official records and place-specific organization/event searches outside Henoko.
implications.visibility_mechanism: Henoko produces durable litigation, statement and NGO records; broad prefecture coding absorbs records without a more precise location.

implications.impact_on_q1_q3: Q1/Q2 and R1 may overstate durable/networked forms; R10/R11 layers are deliberately sampled and cannot be treated as complete sectors.
implications.interpretation_limit: The 121 actors are a value-driven working registry, not a census or a functional population distribution.
implications.local_gap_action: Verify temporary committees, neighborhood groups, former names, continuity and representatives through local holdings.
implications.observed_skew: Okinawa-local actors are 57/121 (47.1%); registry visibility is concentrated in citizen networks/groups and web-visible domestic/international NGOs.
implications.online_gap_action: Resolve aliases, defunct sites, directories, membership pages and event lists for under-visible functional forms.
implications.visibility_mechanism: Named, incorporated or networked actors are easier to identify than short-lived committees, informal neighborhood groups and legacy names.

implications.impact_on_q1_q3: Q2 bridge-actor claims and Q3 issue-linkage comparisons may privilege already explicit base/environment/international framing.
implications.interpretation_limit: Issue-tag counts indicate documented association, not issue salience, effort or public support.
implications.local_gap_action: Use local newsletters, issue campaigns and newspaper databases where organizational issue framing is not indexed online.
implications.observed_skew: Base politics, environment and transnational issue groups have the broadest actor coverage; collective action, external-network and several life-safety subtopics are thinner.
implications.online_gap_action: Target labor, women/human-rights, health, groundwater, noise, welfare and local-autonomy organization records.
implications.visibility_mechanism: Project search paths and high-documentation controversies yield more explicit issue labels than diffuse welfare, labor, gender and health work.

implications.impact_on_q1_q3: All three questions inherit survival, institutional-record and web-search bias; event/relationship modules are especially sensitive.
implications.interpretation_limit: Failed archive does not mean evidence is absent; successful archive does not mean the source proves every coded claim.
implications.local_gap_action: Retrieve print or database copies only where reasonable online routes are exhausted or the source was never public online.
